method.method_draft: Use signed geometric area. From the image, identify one upper semicircle from x = -1 to x = 1 with highest point y = 1, so it has radius 1 and lies above the x-axis. Identify the second semicircle from x = 1 to x = 3 with lowest point y = -1, so it also has radius 1 and lies below the x-axis. From the text, use the requested interval -1 to 3 and the fact that the graph consists of these two semicircles. The integral equals area above the x-axis minus area below the x-axis: (1/2)π(1)^2 - (1/2)π(1)^2 = 0.

method.method_draft: Use symmetry/translation cancellation. From the image, observe that the left arc is the upper semicircle of radius 1 centered at x = 0, while the right arc is the same semicircle shifted 2 units right and reflected below the x-axis, centered at x = 2. From the text, split the requested integral as ∫[-1,1] f(x) dx + ∫[1,3] f(x) dx. Pair each point x in [-1,1] with x + 2 in [1,3]; the image shows f(x + 2) = -f(x). Therefore the two integrals are negatives of each other, so their sum is 0.
